title: Tanzanian Beef Stew
community: The everyday meat stew enjoyed nationwide
author: Mama Salima
desc: Mchuzi wa Nyama — Tanzania's foundational beef stew. Beef simmered low and slow with tomatoes, onions, garlic, ginger, and Tanzanian spices until the sauce is rich, thick, and the meat is falling-tender. The stew that accompanies ugali and rice at every Tanzanian table.
longDesc: Mchuzi wa Nyama is the backbone of Tanzanian everyday cooking — the rich, slow-cooked beef stew that appears alongside ugali and rice at every family meal, every mama lishe lunch counter, and every celebration table. The spicing is warm rather than hot — cumin, coriander, and a touch of pilipili give it depth without fire.
steps: Brown beef in batches in hot oil. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, cook onions until deeply golden — 8 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, and all spices. Stir 1 minute.
Add tomatoes. Cook 8—10 minutes until completely broken down and thick.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Cover and simmer 45—55 minutes until meat is very tender.
chefTips: Bone-in beef adds far more flavour to the sauce.
The tomato-onion base must be cooked until completely reduced before adding water.
Low and slow — rushing produces tough, dry meat.
commonMistakes: Adding water before the tomato base is reduced.
cookingScience: Bone-in beef releases collagen from the bones during slow cooking — this converts to gelatin, giving the sauce a silky, rich body impossible to achieve with boneless meat alone.
sustainabilityTips: Local Tanzanian beef from smallholder farmers.
healthBenefits: Collagen from bone broth supports joints.
culturalNote: Mchuzi wa Nyama is the taste of home for every Tanzanian — the stew that mothers make and children grow up eating. Its smell filling a house means a meal is coming and all is well.
